what: PowerResult.growth_callable(k_index) in power.py: wraps the solver's own matter delta as a growth(a) -> D(a) callable normalised to D(1) = 1, which is the interface HMcode2020 already expects.
why: HMcode was reading sigma.linear_growth - a single-fluid ODE that runs 1.86% high at z = 0 against CAMB's delta_tot - while the perturbation solver runs 0.28%. The solver is the more accurate of the two by 6.6x, and PowerResult.growth() showed the data was already there.

bugs_found_while_wiring_it.interp_axis: np.interp requires an ascending x axis, and a = 1/(1+z) runs opposite to z. Sorting by z handed it a descending axis, which silently interpolated against the wrong end: ratios came out as 0.0128 at z = 0 and 1938 at z = 500.
bugs_found_while_wiring_it.normalisation_reference: a false alarm in my own test script. g(a) is already normalised to D(1) = 1 while the CAMB column was normalised at z = 100, so every z showed the same constant 0.0128 - that is D(z=100)/D(1) = 1/78, the value of delta_tot at z = 0.

verdict: the input HMcode sees goes from 1.86% error to 0.33%, a 5.6x improvement. Option A is closed. It does not move the nonlinear gap itself (27.5%), which is a separate HMcode problem and the next item.
